subject: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler options - ACME follow-up
message_1_subject: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler options - ACME follow-up
message_1_body:
Thanks for taking the time today - good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

Summary of requirements we captured:
- Peak qPS: ~250 (anticipated ramp over next 12 months)
- Typical daily tokens: ~50k tokens/day
- Latency SLO target: p95 <= 200ms for single-turn generative calls
- Security: customer-managed keys (KMS) and VPC private deployment considered for sensitive workloads

How we think about the competitive tradeoffs (high level):
- Hyperscaler reserved instances / managed endpoints:
  - Pros: broad ecosystem integrations, potentially lower raw per-GPU list price
  - Cons: transient capacity availability during bursts, limited unit economics visibility, fewer inference-specific optimizations (KV cache, continuous batching, attention kernels tuned for LLM serving)
- Redwood Dedicated:
  - Pros: reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and capacity guarantees, smart batching/caching to reduce per-token cost, telemetry for token-level cost/latency, SLA-backed uptime
  - Cons: commitment required for reserved capacity (we offer flexible burst and autoscale policies to mitigate)

Proposed tests for a short POC (we can scope to 1-2 weeks):
1) Baseline throughput test: run your model on our Dedicated pool and on a hyperscaler managed endpoint with same model variant; measure sustained qPS and p95 latencies
2) Burst & failover test: validate burst capacity behavior and automated fallback when reserved pool is saturated
3) Cost/runbook comparison: show per-token cost at your observed load and suggest batching/quantization options to hit cost targets

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_vs_Hyperscaler_V1.pdf (high-level comparison), ACME_MAP.xlsx (mutual action plan template)

Next steps:
- Confirm POC scope and success criteria (we suggested the three tests above)
- Share any specific models and input sizes you want validated
- Schedule a technical deep dive with Ben Carter (SE) to align on test harness and endpoints

Thanks - I can be flexible on timing next week for the deep dive.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

message_3_subject: Re: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler options - ACME follow-up
message_3_body:
Hi Derek - quick answers to your questions (and happy to expand on the call):

1) Capacity guarantees:
- Reserved pools are sized to a guaranteed baseline throughput (we define in the MSA appendix). For example, a 4x A100 reserved pool typically guarantees X qPS for the model sizes you indicated; we size based on your p95 target and token lengths.
- Burst capacity: we support short bursts up to 2x baseline for traffic spikes (configurable). Bursts are not guaranteed long-term and are billed as usage over the committed baseline.

2) Billing model:
- Reserved capacity = monthly committed fee (discounted unit price) + metered usage for burst/overages. Typical terms are 12 months for Dedicated contracts; we can discuss 6-month pilots for pilots/POCs.

3) SLA:
- We provide SLA language for uptime (example: 99.9% monthly availability for Dedicated control plane + node replace time SLAs). I've attached the SLA PDF (SLA-Redwood-Dedicated.pdf) for your legal/procurement review.

Technical notes relevant to the POC:
- We will instrument token-level telemetry and provide dashboards so you can see per-route latency and cost breakdowns
- Our runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching which often reduces per-token compute for multi-turn flows by 20-60% depending on reuse
- For throughput testing we'll ask you to provide a representative model binary (or pick from our verified catalog if you prefer).

Links: DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/ACME-Redwood-SLA, JIRA for the POC work: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/SUP-7891

Let us know which day for the deep dive and we'll book Ben (SE) + me.

- Camila
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
